Then she said, “Yes, the men came to me, but I didn’t know where they came from.10 5 About the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was dark, the men went out. Where the men went, I don’t know. Pursue them quickly. You may catch up with them.”11✦ 6 But she had brought them up to the roof, and hidden them under the stalks of flax which she had laid in order on the roof.12✦ 7 The men pursued them along the way to the fords of the Jordan River. As soon as those who pursued them had gone out, they shut the gate.1314✦ 8 Before they had lain down, she came up to them on the roof.15 9 She said to the men, “I know that Yahweh has given you the land16, and that the fear of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.1718✦ 10 For we have heard how Yahweh dried up the water19 of the Red Sea before you, when you came out of Egypt; and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you utterly destroyed.2021✦ 11 As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, and there wasn’t any more spirit in any man22, because of you: for Yahweh your God23, he is God in heaven24 above25, and on earth26 beneath.2728✦ 12 Now therefore, please swear to me by Yahweh, since I have dealt kindly with you, that you also will deal kindly with my father’s house, and give me a true sign;2930✦ 13 and that you will save alive my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters, and all that they have, and will deliver our lives from death.”31 14 The men said to her, “Our life for yours, if you don’t talk about this business of ours; and it shall be, when Yahweh gives us the land32, that we will deal kindly and truly with you.”3334 15 Then she let them down by a cord through the window; for her house was on the side of the wall, and she lived on the wall.35✦ 16 She said to them, “Go to the mountain, lest the pursuers find you. Hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers have returned. Afterward, you may go your way.”36 17 The men said to her, “We will be guiltless of this your oath which you’ve made us to swear.37 18 Behold, when we come into the land38, tie this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down. Gather to yourself into the house your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household.39 19 It shall be that whoever goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood40 will be on his head, and we will be guiltless. Whoever is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand is on him.41✦ 20 But if you talk about this business of ours, then we shall be guiltless of your oath which you’ve made us to swear.”42 21 She said, “Let it be as you have said.” She sent them away, and they departed. Then she tied the scarlet line in the window.43 22 They went and came to the mountain, and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had returned. The pursuers sought them all along the way, but didn’t find them.44 23 Then the two men returned, descended from the mountain, crossed the river, and came to Joshua the son of Nun. They told him all that had happened to them.45 24 They said to Joshua, “Truly Yahweh has delivered all the land46 into our hands. Moreover, all the inhabitants of the land melt away before us.”

3

121 Joshua got up early in the morning; and they moved from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel. They camped there before they crossed over.3✦ 2 After three days, the officers went through the middle of the camp;✦ 3 and they commanded the people, saying, “When you see the ark of Yahweh your God4’s covenant5, and the Levitical priests bearing it, then leave your place and follow it.67✦ 4 Yet there shall be a space between you and it of about two thousand cubits by measure—don’t come closer to it—that you may know the way by which you must go; for you have not passed this way before.”8✦ 5 Joshua said to the people, “Sanctify yourselves9; for tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you.”101112✦ 6 Joshua spoke to the priests, saying, “Take up the ark of the covenant13, and cross over before the people.” They took up the ark of the covenant, and went before the people.14✦ 7 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.151617✦ 8 You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant18, saying, ‘When you come to the brink of the water19s of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.’”✦ 9 Joshua said to the children of Israel, “Come here, and hear the words of Yahweh your God20.”21 10 Joshua said, “By this you shall know that the living God22 is among you, and that he will without fail drive the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Hivite, the Perizzite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, and the Jebusite out from before you.2324✦ 11 Behold, the ark of the covenant25 of the Lord26 of all the earth27 passes over before you into the Jordan.✦ 12 Now therefore take twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, for every tribe a man28.✦ 13 It shall be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of Yahweh, the Lord of all the earth29, rest in the waters30 of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The waters that come down from above shall stand in one heap.”31✦ 14 When the people moved from their tents to pass over the Jordan, the priests who bore the ark of the covenant32 being before the people,33✦ 15 and when those who bore the ark had come to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bore the ark had dipped in the edge of the water34 (for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest),35✦ 16 the waters36 which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap a great way off, at Adam37, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over near Jericho.3839404142✦ 17 The priests who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant43 stood firm on dry ground44 in the middle of the Jordan45; and all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the nation had passed completely over the Jordan.

4

12✦1 When all the nation had completely crossed over the Jordan, Yahweh spoke to Joshua, saying,34✦ 2 “Take twelve men out of the people, a man5 out of every tribe,6✦ 3 and command them, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’”7✦ 4 Then Joshua called the twelve men whom he had prepared of the children of Israel, a man8 out of every tribe.9✦ 5 Joshua said to them, “Cross before the ark of Yahweh your God10 into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you pick up a stone and put it on your shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel;111213✦ 6 that this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’14✦ 7 then you shall tell them, ‘Because the waters15 of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant16. When it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones shall be for a memorial to the children of Israel forever.’”1718✦ 8 The children of Israel did as Joshua commanded, and took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as Yahweh spoke to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel. They carried them over with them to the place where they camped, and laid them down there.1920✦ 9 Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan21, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant22 stood; and they are there to this day.23✦ 10 For the priests who bore the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was finished that Yahweh commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses commanded Joshua; and the people hurried and passed over.2425✦ 11 When all the people had completely crossed over, Yahweh’s ark crossed over with the priests in the presence of the people.2627✦ 12 The children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed before the children of Israel, as Moses spoke to them.28✦ 13 About forty thousand men, ready and armed for war, passed over before Yahweh to battle, to the plains of Jericho.2930✦ 14 On that day, Yahweh magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they feared him, as they feared Moses, all the days of his life.31 15 Yahweh spoke to Joshua, saying,32 16 “Command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, that they come up out of the Jordan.”33 17 Joshua therefore commanded the priests, saying, “Come up out of the Jordan!”34 18 When the priests who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant35 had come up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet had been lifted up to the dry ground, the waters36 of the Jordan returned to their place, and went over all its banks, as before.373839✦ 19 The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.40 20 Joshua set up those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, in Gilgal.41✦ 21 He spoke to the children of Israel, saying, “When your children ask their fathers in time to come42, saying, ‘What do these stones mean?’43✦ 22 Then you shall let your children know, saying, ‘Israel came over this Jordan on dry land44.45✦ 23 For Yahweh your God46 dried up the waters47 of the Jordan from before you until you had crossed over, as Yahweh your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up from before us, until we had crossed over,4849✦ 24 that all the peoples of the earth50 may know that Yahweh’s hand is mighty, and that you may fear51 Yahweh your God52 forever.’”

5

12✦1 When all the kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan westward, and all the kings of the Canaanites, who were by the sea, heard how Yahweh had dried up the waters3 of the Jordan from before the children of Israel until we had crossed over, their heart4 melted, and there was no more spirit5 in them, because of the children of Israel.67✦ 2 At that time, Yahweh said to Joshua, “Make flint knives, and circumcise8 again the sons of Israel the second time.”91011✦ 3 Joshua made himself flint knives, and circumcised the sons of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.1213✦ 4 This is the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, who were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness along the way, after they came out of Egypt.14 5 For all the people who came out were circumcised; but all the people who were born in the wilderness along the way as they came out of Egypt had not been circumcised.15✦ 6 For the children of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness until all the nation, even the men of war who came out of Egypt, were consumed, because they didn’t listen to Yahweh’s voice. Yahweh swore to them that he wouldn’t let them see the land16 which Yahweh swore to their fathers that he would give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.1718✦ 7 Their children, whom he raised up in their place, were circumcised by Joshua, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not circumcised them on the way.19✦ 8 When they were done circumcising the whole nation, they stayed in their places in the camp until they were healed.20✦ 9 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” Therefore the name of that place was called Gilgal to this day.2122 10 The children of Israel encamped in Gilgal. They kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Jericho.23✦ 11 They ate unleavened cakes and parched grain of the produce of the land24 on the next day after the Passover, in the same day.25✦ 12 The manna ceased on the next day, after they had eaten of the produce of the land26. The children of Israel didn’t have manna any more, but they ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.27✦ 13 When Joshua was by Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man28 stood in front of him with his sword drawn29 in his hand. Joshua went to him and said to him, “Are you for us, or for our enemies?”30✦ 14 He said, “No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army31.” Joshua fell on his face to the earth32, and worshiped, and asked him, “What does my lord say to his servant?”3334✦ 15 The prince of Yahweh’s army said to Joshua, “Take off your sandals, for the place on which you stand is holy35.” Joshua did so.

6

12✦1 Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the children of Israel. No one went out, and no one came in.✦ 2 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Behold, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and the mighty men of valor.34✦ 3 All of your men of war shall march around the city, going around the city once. You shall do this six days.5✦ 4 Seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark. On the seventh day, you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.67✦ 5 It shall be that when they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; then the city wall will fall down flat, and the people shall go up, every man8 straight in front of him.”9✦ 6 Joshua the son of Nun called the priests, and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant10, and let seven priests bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before Yahweh’s ark.”1112✦ 7 They said to the people, “Advance! March around the city, and let the armed men pass on before Yahweh’s ark.”1314✦ 8 It was so, that when Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns before Yahweh advanced and blew the trumpets, and the ark of Yahweh’s covenant15 followed them.1617✦ 9 The armed men went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the ark went after them. The trumpets sounded as they went.1819✦ 10 Joshua commanded the people, saying, “You shall not shout nor let your voice be heard, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then you shall shout.”20✦ 11 So he caused Yahweh’s ark to go around the city, circling it once. Then they came into the camp, and stayed in the camp.2122✦ 12 Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up Yahweh’s ark.2324✦ 13 The seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns in front of Yahweh’s ark went on continually, and blew the trumpets. The armed men went in front of them. The rear guard came after Yahweh’s ark. The trumpets sounded as they went.2526✦ 14 The second day they marched around the city once, and returned into the camp. They did this six days.27✦ 15 On the seventh day, they rose early at the dawning of the day, and marched around the city in the same way seven times. On this day only they marched around the city seven times.28✦ 16 At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, “Shout, for Yahweh has given you the city!2930✦ 17 The city shall be devoted, even it and all that is in it, to Yahweh. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live31, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.3233✦ 18 But as for you, only keep yourselves from what is devoted to destruction, lest when you have devoted it, you take of the devoted thing; so you would make the camp of Israel accursed and trouble it.34✦ 19 But all the silver, gold, and vessels of bronze and iron are holy to Yahweh. They shall come into Yahweh’s treasury.”3536✦ 20 So the people shouted and the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat37, so that the people went up into the city, every man38 straight in front of him, and they took the city.3940✦ 21 They utterly destroyed all that was in the city41, both man42 and woman43, both young and old, and ox, sheep, and donkey, with the edge of the sword.44✦ 22 Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house, and bring the woman45 and all that she has out from there, as you swore to her.”46 23 The young men who were spies went in, and brought out Rahab with her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that she had. They also brought out all of her relatives, and they set them outside of the camp of Israel.47 24 They burned the city with fire, and all that was in it. Only they put the silver, the gold, and the vessels of bronze and of iron into the treasury of Yahweh’s house.4849✦ 25 But Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that she had, Joshua saved alive. She lives in the middle of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.50 26 Joshua comman51ded them with an oath at that time, saying, “Cursed is the man before Yahweh who rises up and builds this city Jericho. With the loss of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and with the loss of his youngest son he will set up its gates.”52535455✦ 27 So Yahweh was with Joshua; and his fame was in all the land.

7

11 But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the devoted things; for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the devoted things. Therefore Yahweh’s anger burned against the children of Israel.234 2 Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth Aven, on the east side of Bethel, and spoke to them, saying, “Go up and spy out the land.” The men went up and spied out Ai.56✦ 3 They returned to Joshua, and said to him, “Don’t let all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Don’t make all the people to toil there, for there are only a few of them.”7✦ 4 So about three thousand men of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.✦ 5 The men of Ai struck about thirty-six men of them. They chased them from before the gate even to Shebarim, and struck them at the descent. The hearts of the people melted, and became like water8.910✦ 6 Joshua tore his clothes, and fell to the earth11 on his face before Yahweh’s ark until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust12 on their heads.1314✦ 7 Joshua said, “Alas, Lord15 Yahweh, why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to cause us to perish? I wish that we had been content and lived beyond the Jordan!1617✦ 8 Oh, Lord18, what shall I say, after Israel has turned their backs before their enemies?19✦ 9 For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and will surround us, and cut off our name from the earth20. What will you do for your great name?”21✦ 10 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Get up! Why have you fallen on your face like that?2223 11 Israel has sinned. Yes, they have even transgressed my covenant24 which I commanded them. Yes, they have even taken some of the devoted things, and have also stolen, and also deceived. They have even put it among their own stuff.25 12 Therefore the children of Israel can’t stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted for destruction. I will not be with you any more, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.26 13 Get up! Sanctify the people, and say, ‘Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, for Yahweh, the God27 of Israel, says, “There is a devoted thing among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you take away the devoted thing from among you.”2829 14 In the morning therefore you shall be brought near by your tribes. It shall be that the tribe which Yahweh selects shall come near by families. The family which Yahweh selects shall come near by households. The household which Yahweh selects shall come near man30 by man.3132✦ 15 It shall be, that he who is taken with the devoted thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed Yahweh’s covenant33, and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”3435 16 So Joshua rose up early in the morning and brought Israel near by their tribes. The tribe of Judah was selected.36✦ 17 He brought near the family of Judah, and he selected the family of the Zerahites. He brought near the family of the Zerahites man37 by man, and Zabdi was selected.38✦ 18 He brought near his household man39 by man, and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was selected.40✦ 19 Joshua said to Achan, “My son, please give glory41 to Yahweh, the God42 of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me now what you have done! Don’t hide it from me!”4344✦ 20 Achan answered Joshua, and said, “I have truly sinned against Yahweh, the God45 of Israel, and this is what I have done.4647✦ 21 When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe48, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, then I coveted them and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.”495051✦ 22 So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. Behold, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.52 23 They took them from the middle of the tent, and brought them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel. They laid them down before Yahweh.5354 24 Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the wedge of gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and all that he had; and they brought them up to the valley of Achor.5556✦ 25 Joshua said, “Why have you troubled us? Yahweh will trouble you today57.” All Israel stoned him with stones, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.5859✦ 26 They raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Yahweh turned from the fierceness of his anger. Therefore the name of that place was called “The valley of Achor” to this day.

8

12✦1 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed. Take all the warriors with you, and arise, go up to Ai3. Behold, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, with his people, his city, and his land4.567✦ 2 You shall do to Ai and her king as you did to Jericho and her king, except you shall take its goods and its livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city behind it.”8✦ 3 So Joshua arose, with all the warriors, to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand men, the mighty men of valor, and sent them out by night.9✦ 4 He commanded them, saying, “Behold, you shall lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Don’t go very far from the city, but all of you be ready.1011✦ 5 I and all the people who are with me will approach the city. It shall happen, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them.12✦ 6 They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city; for they will say, ‘They flee before us, like the first time.’ So we will flee before them,13✦ 7 and you shall rise up from the ambush, and take possession of the city; for Yahweh your God14 will deliver it into your hand.1516✦ 8 It shall be, when you have seized the city, that you shall set the city on fire. You shall do this according to Yahweh’s word. Behold, I have commanded you.”1718✦ 9 Joshua sent them out; and they went to set up the ambush, and stayed between Bethel and Ai on the west side of Ai; but Joshua stayed among the people that night.19✦ 10 Joshua rose up early in the morning, mustered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.20✦ 11 All the people, even the men of war who were with him, went up and came near, and came before the city and encamped on the north side of Ai. Now there was a valley between him and Ai.21✦ 12 He took about five thousand men, and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.22✦ 13 So they set the people, even all the army who was on the north of the city, and their ambush on the west of the city; and Joshua went that night into the middle of the valley.23✦ 14 When the king of Ai saw it, they hurried and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at the time appointed, before the Arabah; but he didn’t know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.24✦ 15 Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness.25✦ 16 All the people who were in the city were called together to pursue after them. They pursued Joshua, and were drawn away from the city.26✦ 17 There was not a man27 left in Ai or Bethel who didn’t go out after Israel. They left the city open, and pursued Israel.28✦ 18 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand.” Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.2930✦ 19 The ambush arose quickly out of their place, and they ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand and entered into the city and took it. They hurried and set the city on fire.31✦ 20 When the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven32, and they had no power to flee this way or that way. The people who fled to the wilderness turned back on the pursuers.33 21 When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city, and that the smoke of the city ascended, then they turned back and killed the men of Ai.34 22 The others came out of the city against them, so they were in the middle of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side. They struck them, so that they let none of them remain or escape.35 23 They captured the king of Ai alive, and brought him to Joshua.36 24 When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness in which they pursued them, and they had all fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.37 25 All that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the people of Ai.38 26 For Joshua didn’t draw back his hand, with which he stretched out the javelin, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.39 27 Israel took for themselves only the livestock and the goods of that city, according to Yahweh’s word which he commanded Joshua.40 28 So Joshua burned Ai and made it a heap forever, even a desolation, to this day.41 29 He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until the evening. At sundown, Joshua commanded, and they took his body down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised a great heap of stones on it that remains to this day.42✦ 30 Then Joshua built an altar to Yahweh, the God43 of Israel, on Mount Ebal44,454647✦ 31 as Moses the servant of Yahweh comman48ded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of uncut stones, on which no one had lifted up any iron. They offered burnt offerings on it to Yahweh and sacrificed peace49 offerings.5051✦ 32 He wrote there on the stones a copy of Moses’ law, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.52✦ 33 All Israel, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark before the Levitical priests, who carried the ark of Yahweh’s covenant53, the foreigner as well as the native; half of them in front of Mount Gerizim, and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of Yahweh had commanded at the first, that they should bless the people of Israel.5455✦ 34 Afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.56✦ 35 There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua didn’t read before all the assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who were among them.

9

1✦1 When all the kings who were beyond the Jordan, in the hill country, and in the lowland, and on all the shore of the great sea in front of Lebanon, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard of it2 2 they gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord.3✦ 3 But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,4✦ 4 they also resorted to a ruse, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks on their donkeys, and old, torn-up and bound up wine skins,5678✦ 5 and old and patched sandals on their feet, and wore old garments. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy.910✦ 6 They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Israel, “We have come from a far country. Now therefore make a covenant with us.”1112✦ 7 The men of Israel said to the Hivites, “What if you live among us? How could we make a covenant with you?”13✦ 8 They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Who are you? Where do you come from?”14✦ 9 They said to him, “Your servants have come from a very far country because of the name of Yahweh your God15; for we have heard of his fame, all that he did in Egypt,1617✦ 10 and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.18✦ 11 Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spoke to us, saying, ‘Take supplies in your hand for the journey, and go to meet them. Tell them, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’19✦ 12 This our bread we took hot for our supplies out of our houses on the day we went out to go to you; but now, behold, it is dry, and has become moldy.20✦ 13 These wine skins, which we filled, were new; and behold, they are torn. These our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.”21✦ 14 The men sampled their provisions, and didn’t ask counsel from Yahweh’s mouth.2223✦ 15 Joshua made peace24 with them, and made a covenant with them, to let them live25. The princes of the congregation swore to them.26✦ 16 At the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were their neighbors, and that they lived among them.27✦ 17 The children of Israel traveled and came to their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.2829✦ 18 The children of Israel didn’t strike them, because the princes of the congregation had sworn to them by Yahweh, the God30 of Israel. All the congregation murmured against the princes.3132✦ 19 But all the princes said to all the congregation, “We have sworn to them by Yahweh, the God33 of Israel. Now therefore we may not touch them.3435✦ 20 We will do this to them, and let them live; lest wrath be on us, because of the oath which we swore to them.”36✦ 21 The princes said to them, “Let them live.” So they became wood cutters and drawers of water37 for all the congregation, as the princes had spoken to them.38✦ 22 Joshua called for them, and he spoke to them, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you live among us?39✦ 23 Now therefore you are cursed, and some of you will never fail to be slaves, both wood cutters and drawers of water4041 for the house of my God42.”43✦ 24 They answered Joshua, and said, “Because your servants were certainly told how Yahweh your God44 commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land45, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you. Therefore we were very afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this thing.4647✦ 25 Now, behold, we are in your hand. Do to us as it seems good48 and right to you to do.”49✦ 26 He did so to them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, so that they didn’t kill them.50✦ 27 That day Joshua made them wood cutters and drawers of water51 for the congregation and for Yahweh’s altar to this day, in the place which he should choose.

12✦1 Now when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai, and had utterly destroyed it; as he had done to Jericho and her king, so he had done to Ai and her king; and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace3 with Israel, and were among them,456✦ 2 they were very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.78✦ 3 Therefore Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,9101112✦ 4 “Come up to me and help me. Let’s strike Gibeon; for they have made peace13 with Joshua and with the children of Israel.”14✦ 5 Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it.15✦ 6 The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Don’t abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly and save us! Help us; for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the hill country have gathered together against us.”16✦ 7 So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and the whole army with him, including all the mighty men of valor.17✦ 8 Yahweh said to Joshua, “Don’t fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. Not a man18 of them will stand before you.”192021✦ 9 Joshua therefore came to them suddenly. He marched from Gilgal all night.22✦ 10 Yahweh confused them before Israel. He killed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth Horon, and struck them to Azekah and to Makkedah.2324✦ 11 As they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beth Horon, Yahweh hurled down great stones from the sky on them to Azekah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword.252627✦ 12 Then Joshua spoke to Yahweh in the day when Yahweh delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel. He said in the sight of Israel, “Sun, stand still on Gibeon28! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!”2930313233✦ 13 The sun stood still34, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn’t this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.3536✦ 14 There was no day like that before it or after it, that Yahweh listened to the voice of a man37; for Yahweh fought for Israel.3839✦ 15 Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.40✦ 16 These five kings fled, and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.41✦ 17 Joshua was told, saying, “The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah.”42✦ 18 Joshua said, “Roll large stones to cover the cave’s entrance, and set men by it to guard them;43✦ 19 but don’t stay there. Pursue your enemies, and attack them from the rear. Don’t allow them to enter into their cities; for Yahweh your God44 has delivered them into your hand.”4546✦ 20 When Joshua and the children of Israel had finished killing them with a very great slaughter until they were consumed, and the remnant which remained of them had entered into the fortified cities,47✦ 21 all the people returned to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace48. None moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.49✦ 22 Then Joshua said, “Open the cave entrance, and bring those five kings out of the cave to me.”50✦ 23 They did so, and brought those five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.51✦ 24 When they brought those kings out to Joshua, Joshua called for all the men of Israel, and said to the chiefs of the men of war who went with him, “Come near. Put your feet on the necks of these kings.” They came near, and put their feet on their necks.52✦ 25 Joshua said to them, “Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for Yahweh will do this to all your enemies against whom you fight.”53545556✦ 26 Afterward Joshua struck them, put them to death, and hanged them on five trees. They were hanging on the trees until the evening.57✦ 27 At the time of the going down of the sun, Joshua commanded, and they took them down off the trees, and threw them into the cave in which they had hidden themselves, and laid great stones on the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.58✦ 28 Joshua took Makkedah on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king. He utterly destroyed it and all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.59✦ 29 Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah, and fought against Libnah.60✦ 30 Yahweh delivered it also, with its king, into the hand of Israel. He struck it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining in it. He did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.6162✦ 31 Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish, and encamped against it, and fought against it.63✦ 32 Yahweh delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel. He took it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with all the souls who were in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.6465✦ 33 Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua struck him and his people, until he had left him no one remaining.6667 34 Joshua passed from Lachish, and all Israel with him, to Eglon; and they encamped against it and fought against it.68✦ 35 They took it on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword. He utterly destroyed all the souls who were in it that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.69✦ 36 Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron; and they fought against it.70✦ 37 They took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king and all its cities, and all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining, according to all that he had done to Eglon; but he utterly destroyed it, and all the souls who were in it.71✦ 38 Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it.72✦ 39 He took it, with its king and all its cities. They struck them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed all the souls who were in it. He left no one remaining. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir, and to its king; as he had done also to Libnah, and to its king.73✦ 40 So Joshua struck all the land, the hill country, the South, the lowland, the slopes, and all their kings. He left no one remaining, but he utterly destroyed all that breathed, as Yahweh, the God74 of Israel, commanded.757677✦ 41 Joshua struck them from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even to Gibeon.78 42 Joshua took all these kings and their land79 at one time because Yahweh, the God80 of Israel, fought for Israel.8182 43 Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.

12✦1 Yahweh spoke to Joshua, saying, “34 2Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Assign the cities of refuge5, of which I spoke to you by Moses,6 3 that the man slayer who kills any person accidentally or unintentionally may flee there. They shall be to you for a refuge from the avenger of blood7.8✦ 4 He shall flee to one of those cities, and shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and declare his case in the ears of the elders9 of that city. They shall take him into the city with them, and give him a place, that he may live among them.10✦ 5 If the avenger of blood11 pursues him, then they shall not deliver up the man slayer into his hand; because he struck his neighbor unintentionally, and didn’t hate him before.12 6 He shall dwell in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days. Then the man slayer shall return, and come to his own city, and to his own house, to the city he fled from.’”13 7 They set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba (also called Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.1415✦ 8 Beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.161718✦ 9 These were the appointed cities for all the children of Israel, and for the alien who lives among them, that whoever kills any person unintentionally might flee there, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood19, until he stands trial before the congregation.

Hasn’t Yahweh gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.323334✦ 15 Yahweh confused Sisera, all his chariots, and all his army, with the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled away on his feet.3536 16 But Barak pursued the chariots and the army to Harosheth of the Gentiles; and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword. There was not a man37 left.38 17 However Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace39 between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.4041 18 Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, “Turn in, my lord42, turn in to me; don’t be afraid.” He came in to her into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.4344 19 He said to her, “Please give me a little water45 to drink; for I am thirsty.” She opened a container of milk, and gave him a drink, and covered him.4647✦ 20 He said to her, “Stand in the door of the tent, and if any man48 comes and inquires of you, and says, ‘Is there any man here?’ you shall say, ‘No.’”49✦ 21 Then Jael, Heber’s wife, took a tent peg50, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him, and struck the pin into his temples, and it pierced through into the ground51, for he was in a deep sleep; so he fainted and died.52✦ 22 Behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man53 whom you seek.” He came to her; and behold, Sisera lay dead, and the tent peg was in his temples.54✦ 23 So God55 subdued Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel on that day.56 24 The hand of the children of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.

12✦1 The children of Israel did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, so Yahweh delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.3✦ 2 The hand of Midian prevailed against Israel; and because of Midian the children of Israel made themselves the dens which are in the mountains, the caves, and the strongholds.4✦ 3 So it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east came up against them.5✦ 4 They encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth6, until you come to Gaza. Because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city, he could not do it by day, but he did it by night.6667✦ 28 When the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was broken down, and the Asherah was cut down that was by it, and the second bull was offered on the altar that was built.68✦ 29 They said to one another, “Who has done this thing?” When they inquired and asked, they said, “Gideon the son of Joash has done this thing.”6970 30 Then the men of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son, that he may die, because he has broken down the altar of Baal, and because he has cut down the Asherah that was by it.”71✦ 31 Joash said to all who stood against him, “Will you contend for Baal? If there is dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the ground, then I’ll know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken.”8384✦ 38 It was so; for he rose up early on the next day, and pressed the fleece together, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water85.86✦ 39 Gideon said to God87, “Don’t let your anger be kindled against me, and I will speak but this once. ↩ ◇ Ephrem the Syrian (365). Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'the Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live' (Deu 30:6), Ephrem reads the heart-circumcision-by-divine-action as the canonical Old-Testament promise of grace fulfilled in the new covenant: what Deu 10:16 commands ('circumcise your heart'), Deu 30:6 promises the Lord himself will accomplish. The same gospel-of-grace structure (command becomes promise) flows through Jer 31:33 and Ez 36:26 into Acts 2's Pentecost. Tewahedo theosis-theology cites Deu 30:6 as the canonical Old-Testament anchor: the Spirit-given heart-circumcision IS theosis — God's own action transforming the human heart to love him with the love that he commands.

↩ ◇ Note. The nearness of the Word. A theological turn within the curse-and-blessing framework: the Torah is not unattainable, not in heaven, not across the sea — it is in your mouth and in your heart. Paul cites this passage in Romans 10:6–8 and applies its language of nearness to the gospel of Christ. The original passage is itself one of the highest moments of Old Testament accessibility theology — God’s word is not esoteric, not reserved for an elite.

↩ ◇ Note. Chazak v’ematz (חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ). “Be strong and courageous.” Moses’ commissioning of Joshua, repeated to Joshua directly in Josh 1:6, 1:9. The phrase becomes the standard formula for transferring leadership in Israelite tradition; David uses it to commission Solomon (1 Chr 22:13, 28:20). It survives in modern Hebrew as a customary blessing — what one says at the conclusion of a stretch of public Torah-reading in the synagogue, marking the completion of one section and the courage required for the next.

↩ ⌘ Hebrew. Tzur (צוּר). “Rock” — one of the divine names in the Song of Moses, used six times in this chapter (vv. 4, 15, 18, 30, 31, 37). The image is geological permanence — the unmoved bedrock against which Israel’s waywardness is measured. Paul invokes the same image in 1 Cor 10:4. The Song of Moses (32:1–43) is one of the oldest pieces of Hebrew poetry, with archaic morphology that probably predates the prose of Deuteronomy by centuries — a poem set into a later prose frame, like an inset jewel.

↩ ✧ Variant. “Sons of God” or “sons of Israel”? One of the most famous textual variants in the Hebrew Bible. The Masoretic Text reads b’nei Yisra’el (“sons of Israel”) — followed by the WEB here. The Dead Sea Scrolls (4QDeutj), the Septuagint, and the Old Latin read b’nei elohim (“sons of God”) or angeloi theou (“angels of God”). The variant matters theologically: the older reading depicts God allotting nations to subordinate divine beings, while keeping Israel for himself (32:9). This more polytheistic-sounding text was likely smoothed by Masoretic transmission. Many modern translations (ESV, NRSV, NABRE) restore the older reading.

↩ ◇ Note. The blessing of Moses. Chapter 33 — Moses’ final blessing on the tribes — opens with one of the oldest Hebrew theophany texts. The Sinai-to-Seir-to-Paran progression maps onto the southern desert geography from which Israelite tradition pictures Yahweh emerging. Habakkuk 3:3 echoes the same itinerary. The phrase “fiery law” (or “fire of law,” esh dat) at the end of v. 2 is textually difficult and probably represents a corruption — the LXX and several manuscripts have a different reading altogether. A reminder of how much of biblical poetry sits at the edge of recoverable text.

↩ ◇ Note. The death of Moses. The narrator’s problem is sharp: how does a book that Moses is traditionally said to have written record his own death? The Talmud (Bava Batra 14b–15a) preserves both options — that Joshua wrote the last eight verses, or that Moses wrote them himself in tears, prophetically. The text’s simple cadence (“and Moses the servant of Yahweh died there… and he was buried in the valley… and no one knows his grave to this day”) is one of the most haunting epitaphs in scripture. Jude 9 records a tradition that the archangel Michael disputed with Satan over the body of Moses — a midrashic expansion preserved in the lost work known as the Assumption of Moses.

↩ ◇ Ephrem the Syrian (365). Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On Moses' burial 'in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day' (Deu 34:6), Ephrem reads the divinely-hidden grave as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Jude 9's account of the archangel Michael's dispute with the devil over Moses' body — preserved in the Assumption of Moses tradition received by the Ethiopian canon. The hidden grave prepares Moses for his Transfiguration appearance with Elijah (Mt 17:3, Lk 9:30-31), suggesting a translation-pattern parallel to Enoch (Gen 5:24) and Elijah (2 Ki 2:11). Tewahedo Astə'arǝgya-Mussē (Translation of Moses) commemorates this hidden-grave tradition; Deu 34:6 + Jude 9 + the Buhe Transfiguration form the canonical triple-witness of Moses' translated-glorified state.

↩ ◇ Note. The closing colophon. The Pentateuch ends with a measured judgment on Moses’ uniqueness: face-to-face knowledge of God, unparalleled signs, mighty hand. The verse establishes a benchmark by which all subsequent prophets are measured — and the negative (“there has not arisen”) opens space for the eschatological hope of one who would. In Christian reading, this verse becomes a key text for the Mosaic typology applied to Jesus (Heb 3:1–6). In Jewish tradition, Maimonides’ Thirteen Principles of Faith enshrine Moses’ unique prophetic standing.

↩ ⌘ Hebrew. Y’hoshu‘a (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ) — “Yahweh saves.” The Hebrew name from which Greek Iēsous (Jesus) descends. Joshua is the first person in the Bible to bear what is, etymologically, the name of Jesus. The book opens with a deliberate compositional move: after the death of Moses, exactly the cadence the Pentateuch closes with (Deut 34:5). The prose is signaling that this book continues the story rather than starting a new one — the Deuteronomistic History (Joshua–2 Kings) reads as a single literary arc.

↩ ◇ Note. The first commandment to a leader. Joshua’s commission opens not with military instruction but with Torah-meditation. The verb hagah (“meditate”) means to murmur or recite under one’s breath — Torah study as a continuous bodily practice, not silent reading. Psalm 1:2 echoes this verse almost verbatim, transferring the leader’s discipline to every righteous person. The juxtaposition is striking: Israel’s most aggressive military campaign begins with an order to recite a book.

↩ ◇ Note. Rahab the Canaanite. A Canaanite woman, a prostitute, who hides Israelite spies and bargains for her family’s survival. The narrative protects her actively — she is the chapter’s moral center despite being a triple outsider (Canaanite, woman, sex worker). Matthew 1:5 lists her in the genealogy of Jesus; Hebrews 11:31 names her among the heroes of faith; James 2:25 cites her alongside Abraham as a model of justifying works. The book of Joshua contains both ḥerem (devoted destruction) and Rahab’s rescue — its theology is more layered than its surface campaign narrative suggests.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). HESHBON intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Joshua 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Numbers 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Joshua 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Numbers 32:37). After the Exile it was taken possession of by the Moabites (Isaiah 15:4; Jeremiah 48:2, 34, 45). The ruins of this town are still seen about 20 miles east of Jordan from the north end of the Dead Sea. There are reservoirs in this district, which are probably the “fishpools” referred to in Cant. 7:4.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). ADAM , THE CITY OF is referred to in Joshua 3:16. It stood “beside Zarethan,” on the west bank of Jordan (1 Kings 4:12). At this city the flow of the water was arrested and rose up “upon an heap” at the time of the Israelites’ passing over (Joshua 3:16).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). JERICHO place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Joshua 3:16). Its site was near the ‘Ain es-Sultan, Elisha’s Fountain (2 Kings 2:19-22), about 5 miles west of Jordan. It was the most important city in the Jordan valley (Numbers 22:1; 34:15), and the strongest fortress in all the land of Canaan. It was the key to Western Palestine. This city was taken in a very remarkable manner by the Israelites (Joshua 6). God gave it into their hands. The city was “accursed” (Hebrews herem, “devoted” to Jehovah), and accordingly (Joshua 6:17; comp. Leviticus 27:28, 29; Deuteronomy 13:16) all the inhabitants and all the spoil of the city were to be destroyed, “only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron” were reserved and “put into the treasury of the house of Jehovah” (Joshua 6:24; comp. Numbers 31:22, 23, 50-54). Only Rahab “and her father’s household, and all that she had,” were preserved from destruction, according to the promise of the spies (Joshua 2:14). In one of the Amarna tablets Adoni-zedec (q.v.) writes to the king of Egypt informing him that the ‘Abiri (Hebrews) had prevailed, and had taken the fortress of Jericho, and were plundering “all the king’s lands.” It would seem that the Egyptian troops had before this been withdrawn from Palestine. This city was given to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18:21), and it was inhabited in the time of the Judges (Judges 3:13; 2 Samuel 10:5). It is not again mentioned till the time of David (2 Samuel 10:5). “Children of Jericho” were among the captives who returned under Zerubbabel Ezra 2:34; Nehemiah 7:36). Hiel (q.v.) the Bethelite attempted to make it once more a fortified city (1 Kings 16:34). Between the beginning and the end of his undertaking all his children were cut off. In New Testament times Jericho stood some distance to the south-east of the ancient one, and near the opening of the valley of Achor. It was a rich and flourishing town, having a considerable trade, and celebrated for the palm trees which adorned the plain around. It was visited by our Lord on his last journey to Jerusalem. Here he gave sight to two blind men (Matthew 20:29-34; Mark 10:46-52), and brought salvation to the house of Zacchaeus the publican (Luke 19:2-10). The poor hamlet of er-Riha, the representative of modern Jericho, is situated some two miles farther to the east. It is in a ruinous condition, having been destroyed by the Turks in 1840. “The soil of the plain,” about the middle of which the ancient city stood, “is unsurpassed in fertility; there is abundance of water for irrigation, and many of the old aqueducts are almost perfect; yet nearly the whole plain is waste and desolate...The climate of Jericho is exceedingly hot and unhealthy. This is accounted for by the depression of the plain, which is about 1,200 feet below the level of the sea.” There were three different Jerichos, on three different sites, the Jericho of Joshua, the Jericho of Herod, and the Jericho of the Crusades. Er-Riha, the modern Jericho, dates from the time of the Crusades. Dr. Bliss has found in a hollow scooped out for some purpose or other near the foot of the biggest mound above the Sultan’s Spring specimens of Amorite or pre-Israelitish pottery precisely identical with what he had discovered on the site of ancient Lachish. He also traced in this place for a short distance a mud brick wall in situ, which he supposes to be the very wall that fell before the trumpets of Joshua. The wall is not far from the foot of the great precipice of Quarantania and its numerous caverns, and the spies of Joshua could easily have fled from the city and been speedily hidden in these fastnesses.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). ZARETAN When the Hebrews crossed the Jordan, as soon as the feet of the priests were dipped in the water, the flow of the stream was arrested. The point of arrest was the “city of Adam beside Zaretan,” probably near Succoth, at the mouth of the Jabbok, some 30 miles up the river from where the people were encamped. There the water “stood and rose upon an heap.” Thus the whole space of 30 miles of the river-bed was dry, that the tribes might pass over (Joshua 3:16, 17; comp. Psalm 104:3).

↩ ◇ Note. The Jordan crossing. The Red Sea miracle (Exod 14) now repeated at the Jordan — a deliberate literary frame around the wilderness generation. Moses led Israel out of Egypt through dry-ground waters; Joshua leads them into the land through dry-ground waters. The Ark of the Covenant replaces Moses’ staff as the agent of the miracle, signaling the transfer of mediation from prophet to cult. The flood-stage timing (3:15) is a historical detail; the upper Jordan blockage at Adam (about 30 km upstream) is geologically plausible — landslides have done it in recorded history (most recently 1927).

↩ ◇ Note. Mass circumcision at Gilgal. The wilderness generation had not been circumcised (5:5) — a striking detail that the text explains by reference to ongoing journey conditions. The mass rite at Gilgal (“rolling place,” a wordplay on the “rolling away” of Egyptian reproach in 5:9) marks the threshold from wilderness wandering to covenantal land-life. The use of flint knives — a Bronze Age anachronism by the late settlement period — preserves an ancient ritual conservatism, like the use of unhewn stones for altars in Exod 20:25.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). KNIFE (1.) Hebrews hereb, “the waster,” a sharp instrument for circumcision (Joshua 5:2, 3, lit. “knives of flint;” comp. Exodus 4:25); a razor (Ezekiel 5:1); a graving tool (Exodus 20:25); an axe (Ezekiel 26:9). (2.) Hebrews maakeleth, a large knife for slaughtering and cutting up food (Genesis 22:6, 10; Proverbs 30:14). (3.) Hebrews sakkin, a knife for any purpose, a table knife (Proverbs 23:2). (4.) Hebrews mahalaph, a butcher’s knife for slaughtering the victims offered in sacrifice (Ezra 1:9). (5.) Smaller knives (Hebrews ta’ar, Jeremiah 36:26) were used for sharpening pens. The pruning-knives mentioned in Isaiah 18:5 (Hebrews mizmaroth) were probably curved knives.

↩ ◇ Note. The commander of Yahweh’s army. One of the more enigmatic theophanies in the Hebrew Bible. The figure is called “commander of Yahweh’s army” (5:14), refuses both human sides of the question (“Are you for us or for our adversaries?” — “No”), and demands Joshua remove his sandals (5:15) — a direct echo of Moses at the burning bush (Exod 3:5). Christian tradition reads the figure as a pre-incarnate Christ; rabbinic tradition reads him as the angel Michael. The narrative leaves the question deliberately open.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). HORN Trumpets were at first horns perforated at the tip, used for various purposes (Joshua 6:4,5). Flasks or vessels were made of horn (1 Samuel 16:1, 13; 1 Kings 1:39). But the word is used also metaphorically to denote the projecting corners of the altar of burnt offerings (Exodus 27:2) and of incense (30:2). The horns of the altar of burnt offerings were to be smeared with the blood of the slain bullock (29:12; Leviticus 4:7-18). The criminal, when his crime was accidental, found an asylum by laying hold of the horns of the altar (1 Kings 1:50; 2:28). The word also denotes the peak or summit of a hill (Isaiah 5:1, where the word “hill” is the rendering of the same Hebrew word). This word is used metaphorically also for strength (Deuteronomy 33:17) and honour (Job 16:15; Lamentations 2:3). Horns are emblems of power, dominion, glory, and fierceness, as they are the chief means of attack and defence with the animals endowed with them (Daniel 8:5, 9; 1 Samuel 2:1; 16:1, 13; 1 Kings 1:39; 22:11; Joshua 6:4, 5; Psalm 75:5, 10; 132:17; Luke 1:69, etc.). The expression “horn of salvation,” applied to Christ, means a salvation of strength, or a strong Saviour (Luke 1:69). To have the horn “exalted” denotes prosperity and triumph (Psalm 89:17, 24). To “lift up” the horn is to act proudly (Zechariah 1:21). Horns are also the symbol of royal dignity and power (Jeremiah 48:25; Zechariah 1:18; Daniel 8:24).

↩ ◇ Note. Jericho. Excavations at Tell es-Sultan (the site of ancient Jericho) have produced a famously contested archaeological record. Kathleen Kenyon’s mid-20th-century excavations dated the destruction layer to ~1550 BCE — significantly before any plausible Joshua timeframe (~1400–1200 BCE depending on chronology). Bryant Wood’s reanalysis in the 1990s argued for a later date (~1400 BCE) based on pottery typology, more consistent with the biblical narrative. The matter remains unsettled. Whatever the historical layer, the textual narrative is theologically focused: the wall falls because Israel marches and trumpets, not because they breach it — the city is given, not taken.

↩ ‖ Cite. Cross-references. Heb 11:30.

↩ ⌘ Hebrew. Ḥerem (חֵרֶם). “Devoted to destruction.” One of the most theologically and ethically difficult concepts in the Hebrew Bible — the absolute ban requiring destruction of all life in a captured city. Modern scholarship reads ḥerem through several lenses: as ancient Near Eastern total-war rhetoric (paralleled in the 9th-c. BCE Mesha Stele, where King Mesha of Moab claims to have devoted the Israelites of Nebo to ḥerem); as a theological category about radical separation from the land’s previous religious systems (Deut 7:1–6); or as a literary trope of completed conquest. The category troubled later Jewish and Christian readers alike — the rabbis declared the original ethnic referents extinct (and so the law inoperative); Christian readers have wrestled with it from Origen forward.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). ZABDI gift of Jehovah. (1.) An ancestor of Achan (Joshua 7:1, 17, 18). He is probably the “Zimri” of 1 Chronicles 2:6. (2.) A Benjamite (1 Chronicles 8:19). (3.) Called “the Shiphmite,” one of David’s officers, who had charge of his vineyards (1 Chronicles 27:27). (4.) A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Nehemiah 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chronicles 9:15), and Zaccur (Nehemiah 12:35).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). BETH-AVEN house of nothingness; i.e., “of idols”, a place in the mountains of Benjamin, east of Bethel (Joshua 7:2; 18:12; 1 Samuel 13:5). In Hos. 4:15; 5:8; 10:5 it stands for “Bethel” (q.v.), and it is so called because it was no longer the “house of God,” but “the house of idols,” referring to the calves there worshipped.

↩ ◇ Note. The Achan story. A counter-narrative to Rahab. Where the Canaanite woman is saved with her household, the Israelite man is destroyed with his. Both stories turn on the question of ḥerem: Rahab is preserved from the ban by oath; Achan violates the ban and falls under it. The two stories together suggest that the narrative’s moral lines run through individuals, not through ethnic categories. The Hebrew of v. 21 specifies a “Shinar mantle” — Shinar being the biblical name for Babylonia, an early instance of the “Babylon as locus of luxurious idolatry” motif that recurs throughout scripture.

↩ ◇ Note. The Ebal altar. Joshua follows the Deuteronomic command (Deut 27:4–8) to build an altar on Mount Ebal upon entering the land. Adam Zertal’s excavations on Mount Ebal in the 1980s uncovered a large rectangular stone structure dated to the early Iron Age, which he identified as Joshua’s altar. The identification remains contested — alternative readings have been proposed (a watchtower, a different cultic installation) — but the site has become a focal point in the archaeology of early Israelite religion. A small lead curse tablet (the “Mount Ebal lead tablet,” published 2022) was recovered nearby, with a contested early Hebrew inscription invoking divine curse.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). ADONI-ZEDEC Lord of justice or righteousness, was king in Jerusalem at the time when the Israelites invaded Palestine (Joshua 10:1,3). He formed a confederacy with the other Canaanitish kings against the Israelites, but was utterly routed by Joshua when he was engaged in besieging the Gibeonites. The history of this victory and of the treatment of the five confederated kings is recorded in Joshua 10:1-27. (Comp. Deuteronomy 21:23). Among the Tell Amarna tablets (see EGYPT) are some very interesting letters from Adoni-zedec to the King of Egypt. These illustrate in a very remarkable manner the history recorded in Joshua 10, and indeed throw light on the wars of conquest generally, so that they may be read as a kind of commentary on the book of Joshua. Here the conquering career of the Abiri (i.e., Hebrews) is graphically described: “Behold, I say that the land of the king my Lord is ruined”, “The wars are mighty against me”, “The Hebrew chiefs plunder all the king’s lands”, “Behold, I the chief of the Amorites am breaking to pieces.” Then he implores the king of Egypt to send soldiers to help him, directing that the army should come by sea to Ascalon or Gaza, and thence march to Wru-sa-lim (Jerusalem) by the valley of Elah.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). AI ruins. (1.) One of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Joshua 10:1; Genesis 12:8; 13:3). It was the scene of Joshua’s defeat, and afterwards of his victory. It was the second Canaanite city taken by Israel (Joshua 7:2-5; 8:1-29). It lay rebuilt and inhibited by the Benjamites (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32; 11:31). It lay to the east of Bethel, “beside Beth-aven.” The spot which is most probably the site of this ancient city is Haiyan, 2 miles east from Bethel. It lay up the Wady Suweinit, a steep, rugged valley, extending from the Jordan valley to Bethel. (2.) A city in the Ammonite territory (Jeremiah 49:3). Some have thought that the proper reading of the word is Ar (Isaiah 15:1).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). GIBEON hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” (Joshua 10:2). Its inhabitants were Hivites (11:19). It lay within the territory of Benjamin, and became a priest-city (18:25; 21:17). Here the tabernacle was set up after the destruction of Nob, and here it remained many years till the temple was built by Solomon. It is represented by the modern el-Jib, to the south-west of Ai, and about 5 1/2 miles north-north-west of Jerusalem. A deputation of the Gibeonites, with their allies from three other cities (Joshua 9;17), visited the camp at Gilgal, and by false representations induced Joshua to enter into a league with them, although the Israelites had been specially warned against any league with the inhabitants of Canaan (Exodus 23:32; 34:12; Numbers 33:55; Deuteronomy 7:2). The deception practised on Joshua was detected three days later; but the oath rashly sworn “by Jehovah God of Israel” was kept, and the lives of the Gibeonites were spared. They were, however, made “bondmen” to the sanctuary (Joshua 9:23). The most remarkable incident connected with this city was the victory Joshua gained over the kings of Palestine (Joshua 10:16-27). The battle here fought has been regarded as “one of the most important in the history of the world.” The kings of southern Canaan entered into a confederacy against Gibeon (because it had entered into a league with Joshua) under the leadership of Adoni-zedec, king of Jerusalem, and marched upon Gibeon with the view of taking possession of it. The Gibeonites entreated Joshua to come to their aid with the utmost speed. His army came suddenly upon that of the Amorite kings as it lay encamped before the city. It was completely routed, and only broken remnants of their great host found refuge in the fenced cities. The five confederate kings who led the army were taken prisoners, and put to death at Makkedah (q.v.). This eventful battle of Beth-horon sealed the fate of all the cities of Southern Palestine. Among the Amarna tablets is a letter from Adoni-zedec (q.v.) to the king of Egypt, written probably at Makkedah after the defeat, showing that the kings contemplated flight into Egypt. This place is again brought into notice as the scene of a battle between the army of Ish-bosheth under Abner and that of David led by Joab. At the suggestion of Abner, to spare the effusion of blood twelve men on either side were chosen to decide the battle. The issue was unexpected; for each of the men slew his fellow, and thus they all perished. The two armies then engaged in battle, in which Abner and his host were routed and put to flight (2 Samuel 2:12-17). This battle led to a virtual truce between Judah and Israel, Judah, under David, increasing in power; and Israel, under Ish-bosheth, continually losing ground. Soon after the death of Absalom and David’s restoration to his throne his kingdom was visited by a grievous famine, which was found to be a punishment for Saul’s violation (2 Samuel 21:2, 5) of the covenant with the Gibeonites (Joshua 9:3-27). The Gibeonites demanded blood for the wrong that had been done to them, and accordingly David gave up to them the two sons of Rizpah (q.v.) and the five sons of Michal, and these the Gibeonites took and hanged or crucified “in the hill before the Lord” (2 Samuel 21:9); and there the bodies hung for six months (21:10), and all the while Rizpah watched over the blackening corpses and “suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.” David afterwards removed the bones of Saul and Jonathan at Jabeshgilead (21:12, 13). Here, “at the great stone,” Amasa was put to death by Joab (2 Samuel 20:5-10). To the altar of burnt-offering which was at Gibeon, Joab (1 Kings 2:28-34), who had taken the side of Adonijah, fled for sanctuary in the beginning of Solomon’s reign, and was there also slain by the hand of Benaiah. Soon after he came to the throne, Solomon paid a visit of state to Gibeon, there to offer sacrifices (1 Kings 3:4; 2 Chronicles 1:3). On this occasion the Lord appeared to him in a memorable dream, recorded in 1 Kings 3:5-15; 2 Chronicles 1:7-12. When the temple was built “all the men of Israel assembled themselves” to king Solomon, and brought up from Gibeon the tabernacle and “all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle” to Jerusalem, where they remained till they were carried away by Nebuchadnezzar (2 Kings 24:13).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). HOHAM Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Joshua 10:3, 5, 16-27).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). JAPHIA splendid. (1.) The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Joshua 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Joshua 10:33). (2.) One of the sons of David (2 Samuel 5:15), born in Jerusalem. (3.) A town in the southern boundary of Zebulum (Joshua 19:12); now Yafa, 2 miles south-west of Nazareth.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). LACHISH impregnable, a royal Canaanitish city in the Shephelah, or maritime plain of Palestine (Joshua 10:3, 5; 12:11). It was taken and destroyed by the Israelites (Joshua 10:31-33). It afterwards became, under Rehoboam, one of the strongest fortresses of Judah (2 Chronicles 10:9). It was assaulted and probably taken by Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:14, 17; 19:8; Isaiah 36:2). An account of this siege is given on some slabs found in the chambers of the palace of Koyunjik, and now in the British Museum. The inscription has been deciphered as follows:, “Sennacherib, the mighty king, king of the country of Assyria, sitting on the throne of judgment before the city of Lachish: I gave permission for its slaughter.” (See NINEVEH.) Lachish has been identified with Tell-el-Hesy, where a cuneiform tablet has been found, containing a letter supposed to be from Amenophis at Amarna in reply to one of the Amarna tablets sent by Zimrida from Lachish. This letter is from the chief of Atim (=Etam, 1 Chronicles 4:32) to the chief of Lachish, in which the writer expresses great alarm at the approach of marauders from the Hebron hills. “They have entered the land,” he says, “to lay waste...strong is he who has come down. He lays waste.” This letter shows that “the communication by tablets in cuneiform script was not only usual in writing to Egypt, but in the internal correspondence of the country. The letter, though not so important in some ways as the Moabite stone and the Siloam text, is one of the most valuable discoveries ever made in Palestine” (Conder’s Tell Amarna Tablets, p. 134). Excavations at Lachish are still going on, and among other discoveries is that of an iron blast-furnace, with slag and ashes, which is supposed to have existed B.C. 1500. If the theories of experts are correct, the use of the hot-air blast instead of cold air (an improvement in iron manufacture patented by Neilson in 1828) was known fifteen hundred years before Christ. (See FURNACE.)

↩ ◇ Note. The long day. One of the most dramatic miracle reports in scripture, framed as direct address: Joshua addresses the sun and moon. The book of Jashar (cited in v. 13) is one of about a dozen lost works the Hebrew Bible references — see also 2 Sam 1:18. Modern interpreters split: literal cosmological miracle, atmospheric refraction phenomenon, or poetic hyperbole quoted from a battle song. The text itself acknowledges its unusual character (10:14 — “there was no day like that before it or after it”), and the framing as quotation from a separate poetic source suggests the narrator is preserving an older tradition rather than asserting plain prose history.

↩ ◇ Note. The unfinished conquest. Chapter 13 marks a decisive narrative turn: Joshua is old, the land is not all conquered, and Yahweh tells him to assign the unconquered territories anyway. The book’s second half (chs 13–24) is concerned with land allotment, not with battles. The honest acknowledgment that significant Canaanite presence remained becomes a key theme of the book of Judges, which opens by listing precisely the territories Joshua failed to take. The conquest narrative is internally self-correcting — the Bible itself complicates the simple picture often associated with Joshua.

↩ ◇ Note. Caleb’s portion. The Kenizzite Caleb (a non-Israelite by ancestry — see Num 32:12, Josh 14:6) receives Hebron as his inheritance for fidelity at Kadesh-barnea forty-five years earlier (14:10). The narrative quietly preserves the genealogical complexity of early Israel: a non-Israelite of demonstrated loyalty receives one of the most sacred sites in the land — the patriarchal burial place at Machpelah. The Caleb tradition coexists with the more rigid genealogical boundaries of later texts.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). ADUMMIM the red ones, a place apparently on the road between Jericho and Jerusalem, “on the south side of the torrent” Wady Kelt, looking toward Gilgal, mentioned Joshua 15:7; 18:17. It was nearly half-way between Jerusalem and Jericho, and now bears the name of Tal-at-ed-Dumm. It is supposed to have been the place referred to in the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37). Recently a new carriage-road has been completed, and carriages for the first time have come along this road from Jerusalem.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). EN-SHEMESH fountain of the sun a spring which formed one of the landmarks on the boundary between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:7; 18:17). It was between the “ascent of Adummim” and the spring of En-rogel, and hence was on the east of Jerusalem and of the Mount of Olives. It is the modern ‘Ain-Haud i.e., the “well of the apostles” about a mile east of Bethany, the only spring on the road to Jericho. The sun shines on it the whole day long.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). HINNOM a deep, narrow ravine separating Mount Zion from the so-called “Hill of Evil Counsel.” It took its name from “some ancient hero, the son of Hinnom.” It is first mentioned in Joshua 15:8. It had been the place where the idolatrous Jews burned their children alive to Moloch and Baal. A particular part of the valley was called Tophet, or the “fire-stove,” where the children were burned. After the Exile, in order to show their abhorrence of the locality, the Jews made this valley the receptacle of the offal of the city, for the destruction of which a fire was, as is supposed, kept constantly burning there. The Jews associated with this valley these two ideas, (1) that of the sufferings of the victims that had there been sacrificed; and (2) that of filth and corruption. It became thus to the popular mind a symbol of the abode of the wicked hereafter. It came to signify hell as the place of the wicked. “It might be shown by infinite examples that the Jews expressed hell, or the place of the damned, by this word. The word Gehenna [the Greek contraction of Hinnom] was never used in the time of Christ in any other sense than to denote the place of future punishment.” About this fact there can be no question. In this sense the word is used eleven times in our Lord’s discourses (Matthew 23:33; Luke 12:5; Matthew 5:22, etc.).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). JEBUS trodden hard, or fastness, or “the waterless hill”, the name of the Canaanitish city which stood on Mount Zion (Joshua 15:8; 18:16, 28). It is identified with Jerusalem (q.v.) in Judges 19:10, and with the castle or city of David (1 Chronicles 11:4,5). It was a place of great natural strength, and its capture was one of David’s most brilliant achievements (2 Samuel 5:8).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). NEPHTOAH opened, a fountain and a stream issuing from it on the border between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8, 9; 18:15). It has been identified with ‘Ain Lifta, a spring about 2 1/2 miles north-west of Jerusalem. Others, however, have identified it with ‘Ain’ Atan, on the south-west of Bethlehem, whence water is conveyed through “Pilate’s aqueduct” to the Haram area at Jerusalem.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). REPHAIM , VALLEY OF (Joshua 15:8; 18:16, R.V.). When David became king over all Israel, the Philistines, judging that he would now become their uncompromising enemy, made a sudden attack upon Hebron, compelling David to retire from it. He sought refuge in “the hold” at Adullam (2 Samuel 5:17-22), and the Philistines took up their position in the valley of Rephaim, on the west and south-west of Jerusalem. Thus all communication between Bethlehem and Jerusalem was intercepted. While David and his army were encamped here, there occurred that incident narrated in 2 Samuel 23:15-17. Having obtained divine direction, David led his army against the Philistines, and gained a complete victory over them. The scene of this victory was afterwards called Baalperazim (q.v.). A second time, however, the Philistines rallied their forces in this valley (2 Samuel 5:22). Again warned by a divine oracle, David led his army to Gibeon, and attacked the Philistines from the south, inflicting on them another severe defeat, and chasing them with great slaughter to Gezer (q.v.). There David kept in check these enemies of Israel. This valley is now called el-Bukei’a.
